caption:
Your refusal letter has a code on it. Most people never find out what it means.

Schengen refusals cite numbered grounds. They are terse, bureaucratic and rarely explained — so most applicants reapply without ever understanding what was actually wrong.

That is how people collect a second refusal.

We built a free decoder that translates the grounds into plain English and tells you what typically fixes each one.

slides.headline: YOUR REFUSAL LETTER IS TRYING TO TELL YOU SOMETHING.
slides.note: Refusals cite numbered grounds. Terse, bureaucratic, rarely explained. So people reapply blind.

slides.body: It tells you the category of the problem. Not the whole story — but enough to know what to fix before you try again.
slides.note: Reapplying without decoding it is how a first refusal becomes a second.

slides.headline: WHAT THE GROUNDS USUALLY POINT TO
items: Purpose of the trip not sufficiently established
Justification for the intended stay unclear
Intention to leave before visa expiry not established
slides.footnote: Wording varies by consulate. Always read your own letter.

slides.headline: WHAT PEOPLE DO NEXT
slides.never: Resubmit the same file within days, hoping a different officer sees it differently. The file has not changed, so the outcome usually does not either — and now there are two refusals on record.
slides.instead: Decode the ground. Fix that specific weakness. Rebuild the file so it answers the objection directly. Then apply.
